title: BOM cost rollup, printed-mass model, print-time heuristic and FDM plate packing over STL parts

governing_equations.name: mesh volume (divergence theorem)
governing_equations.description: Signed-tetrahedron sum over the STL triangle soup; exact for a closed, consistently wound mesh (the absolute value is taken).

governing_equations.name: mesh surface area
governing_equations.description: Total triangle area — both sides of every internal wall count, which is what a slicer's perimeters do.

governing_equations.name: printed-mass model
governing_equations.expr: t_shell = perimeters * line_width + top_bottom_layers * layer_h / 2 ;  V_shell = min(V, A * t_shell) ;  printed_g = rho * [V_shell + infill * max(0, V - V_shell)] / 1e6 ;  solid_g = rho * V / 1e6
governing_equations.description: Slicer-style planning estimate: a shell of thickness t_shell over the whole surface plus sparse infill in the remaining core, capped at the solid mass (a part thinner than its own shell prints fully dense). Defaults {perimeters 3, line_width 0.45, layer_h 0.2, top_bottom_layers 4, infill 0.20} give t_shell = 1.75 mm. Stated band +/-30%.

governing_equations.name: print-time heuristic
governing_equations.expr: t_h = printed_g / 12 * speed_factor per part ;  + 0.25 h setup per plate
governing_equations.description: 0.2 mm-layer-class grams-per-hour rule of thumb; stated band +/-50% — the slicer is the real number.

governing_equations.name: cost rollup
governing_equations.expr: unit_cost = printed_g * price_per_kg / 1000 ;  line_cost = unit_cost * qty ;  total = sum(made) + sum(priced buy lines)
governing_equations.description: Buy lines without unit_price are TBD and EXCLUDED from the numeric total; the receipt names how many.

governing_equations.name: thick-section warning
governing_equations.description: The part is mostly bulk solid — consider hollowing or lattice infill.

governing_equations.name: plate packing
governing_equations.expr: first-fit-decreasing (long side desc) shelf packing with 0/90 deg rotation, spacing s to every neighbour and to the bed edges; refuse iff height > bed.z or min(w,d)+2s > bed.y or max(w,d)+2s > bed.x
governing_equations.description: 2-D bin packing on axis-aligned footprint bounding boxes; a part that cannot fit an empty bed refuses the whole job loudly.

assumptions: STLs are binary, watertight and consistently wound; volume/area are geometric truths of the mesh only under that assumption (garbage in => garbage grams).

The printed-mass model smears the top/bottom skin stacks over ALL surfaces at half thickness — a heuristic, since only up/down-facing regions carry them; it is a planning figure with a stated +/-30% band.
Print time is a grams-per-hour heuristic for 0.2 mm layers (band +/-50%); it does not model travel, retraction, or geometry-dependent speed.
Densities come from tools/material_db.json (inline job overrides win); a material with no density from either source is refused.
Packing uses axis-aligned bounding boxes, not true outlines, so a plate can be packable in reality yet refused here (conservative), never the reverse.
Bookkeeping, not physics: no strength, no thermal, no slicer emulation.

boundary_conditions.fixtures: not applicable — the printable envelope is bed {x, y, z} (default 220 x 220 x 250 mm) with spacing_mm (default 5) to neighbours and edges.

outputs.plates[].parts[].x_mm/y_mm/w_mm/d_mm: mm (bed frame, part corner at its placed origin)

discretization.method: closed form over the triangle soup
discretization.element: STL triangles (float64); packing on footprint bounding boxes
discretization.notes: Deterministic: FFD order is (long side desc, name, instance); no clock (date is a job string), no RNG.

additional_pins: tools/tests/test_aux_tools.py (gate suite: plate STLs, staleness guards)
validation.ground_truth: Analytic boxes written as 12-triangle binary STLs, arithmetic stated in the pin: 30x20x10 mm box -> V = 6000 mm^3, A = 2(600+200+300) = 2200 mm^2, PLA rho 1240 -> solid 7.44 g; t_shell = 3x0.45 + 4x0.2/2 = 1.75 mm, V_shell = min(6000, 2200x1.75 = 3850) = 3850, printed volume 3850 + 0.2x2150 = 4280 mm^3 -> printed 5.3072 g, cost 5.3072 x 25/1000, time 5.3072/12 h + 0.25 h/plate; a 50 mm cube (V 125000, A 15000 -> printed 46000 mm^3 = 57.04 g vs solid 155 g) fires the thick-section warning; a 30x20x1 mm plate (A t_shell 2275 > V 600) is capped at its solid mass; qty 4 of the box on a 60x60 bed at 5 mm spacing packs 2 per plate -> 2 plates and 2 x 0.25 h setup; a 300 mm tall part refuses the job (exit 1).

error_band.volume_and_area: exact to 1e-6 relative (float64 on axis-aligned triangles) — measured 0.0
error_band.mass_cost_time: exact to the receipt's rounding (3-4 decimals) — measured within 5e-4
error_band.packing: exact plate count and in-bed, non-overlapping placements — measured as derived
error_band.determinism: stdout receipt byte-identical across reruns (paths are absolute but stable within one run directory) — measured identical

validation.direction: volume/area are unbiased mesh truths; printed_g and print time are heuristics with stated +/-30% / +/-50% planning bands (no direction claimed); packing is conservative (bounding boxes).

caveats: printed_g and print_time_h are PLANNING figures with stated bands; the slicer is the real number.
A non-watertight or inconsistently wound STL gives a wrong volume with no warning here — gate `watertight` on the export receipt first.
Bounding-box packing over-estimates plate count for L-shaped or nested parts.
Failure (bad job, unfit part, missing density) exits 1 with {ok:false, error} — this tool has its own main and does not distinguish exit 1 from exit 2.
The plate layout PNG needs matplotlib; set emit_plates:false for a numpy-only run.

limits_of_validity.regime: closed binary-STL parts in mm; FDM plate packing on a rectangular bed
limits_of_validity.resolution: mass model: parts thinner than t_shell print fully dense (cap applied); infill fraction in [0,1]

sources.title: Divergence-theorem volume of a closed triangle mesh
sources.ref: Zhang & Chen, 'Efficient feature extraction for 2D/3D objects in mesh representation', Proc. ICIP 2001 (signed tetrahedron volume sum)

sources.title: tools/material_db.json densities
sources.used_for: rho for solid and printed mass

sources.title: Slicer shell/infill decomposition (perimeters x line width + top/bottom layers, sparse infill in the core)
sources.ref: PrusaSlicer / Bambu Studio documentation of perimeters, top/bottom solid layers and infill density — the model in this tool is a stated simplification of that decomposition
sources.used_for: printed_mass_g and the t_shell default 1.75 mm
